c043.front: UNION vs UNION ALL: how do they differ?
c043.back: UNION removes duplicates (it used to sort along the way). UNION ALL keeps all rows and is cheaper, because it does not look for duplicates.
c043.try_sql:
-- UNION removes duplicates, UNION ALL keeps all rows
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT department_id FROM employees UNION SELECT department_id FROM departments)) AS u,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT department_id FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT department_id FROM departments)) AS u_all
FROM dual;

c044.front: ORDER BY in a compound query (for example with UNION)?
c044.back: Only once, at the very end. Use column names or aliases from the first SELECT, or position numbers, for example ORDER BY 1.
c044.try_sql:
-- One ORDER BY at the very end: an alias from the first SELECT or a position number
SELECT last_name AS name FROM employees
UNION
SELECT customer_name FROM customers
ORDER BY 1;

c045.front: Where do the column names of a compound query's result come from?
c045.try_sql:
-- The result column is called NAME (from the first SELECT), not CUSTOMER
SELECT last_name AS name FROM employees
UNION
SELECT customer_name AS customer FROM customers;

c046.back: When comparing rows, NULL is treated as equal to another NULL (unlike with =). For example UNION keeps only one NULL.
c046.try_sql:
-- Grant has department NULL, dual adds a second NULL: the result has only one
SELECT department_id FROM employees
UNION
SELECT NULL FROM dual
ORDER BY 1;

c047.front: In what order do the set operators work?
c047.back: They all have the same precedence and run in order, from left to right. Parentheses let you change the order.

c406.back: INTERSECT returns rows without duplicates and matches NULL to NULL. IN and a join use =, so NULL never matches, and a join can repeat rows.

c407.front: A UNION B INTERSECT C in Oracle 19c?
c407.back: It is evaluated as (A UNION B) INTERSECT C: the same precedence, left to right. Standard SQL would evaluate INTERSECT first.

c408.back: A MINUS B ≠ B MINUS A: the order matters. The result has no duplicates. A NULL in B removes only the rows with NULL in A; it does not wipe the whole result, as NOT IN does.

c409.front: EXCEPT, MINUS ALL, INTERSECT ALL in 19c?
c409.back: 19c does not have them: there are only UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT and MINUS. EXCEPT and the ALL versions arrived in 21c.

c410.front: ORDER BY with an alias from the second SELECT, or with a table alias (e.col)?
c410.back: Both fail with ORA-00904. Use a name or alias from the first SELECT, or a position number.
c410.try_sql:
-- An alias from the second SELECT in ORDER BY: error
SELECT last_name AS name FROM employees
UNION
SELECT customer_name AS cust FROM customers
ORDER BY cust;

c411.back: 01789: the SELECTs return different numbers of columns. 01790: you mix type groups in the same position (for example NUMBER and VARCHAR2). Fix: add NULL as the missing column, or use TO_CHAR.

c1450.front: INTERSECT on two columns: when does a row get through?
c1450.back: When the whole row (both values together) is in both parts. (20, Sales Rep) from Russell and from Partners matches, although they are different people: rows are compared, not people.
c1450.try_sql:
-- Russell (105) and Partners (106) are different people, but the row (20, Sales Rep) is the same
SELECT department_id, job_title FROM employees WHERE employee_id = 105
INTERSECT
SELECT department_id, job_title FROM employees WHERE employee_id = 106;

c1451.front: INTERSECT vs IN when the column has NULLs?
c1451.back: INTERSECT treats NULL as equal to NULL and can return a row with NULL. IN uses =, so NULL never matches. Example: country_code INTERSECT ... returns US and NULL, while IN returns only US.

c1452.front: order_date INTERSECT DATE '2024-03-31', when the order was placed at 23:30?
c1452.back: No row: set operators compare the whole date together with the time, and 23:30 is not midnight. Use TRUNC(order_date) in that part of the query.

c1453.front: Does A UNION B INTERSECT C in Oracle mean A UNION (B INTERSECT C)?
c1453.back: No. All set operators have the same precedence and run from top to bottom: (A UNION B) INTERSECT C, in 19c and still in 23ai. Force another order with parentheses.
c1453.try_sql:
-- Without parentheses: (A UNION B) INTERSECT C = 10, 20, 30. With parentheses, 40 appears too
SELECT department_id FROM departments
UNION SELECT department_id FROM employees
INTERSECT SELECT department_id FROM employees WHERE salary > 10000;
SELECT department_id FROM departments
UNION (SELECT department_id FROM employees
       INTERSECT SELECT department_id FROM employees WHERE salary > 10000);

c1454.back: 19c: ORA-00928 missing SELECT keyword. 21c and 23ai: they work. MINUS ALL subtracts occurrences (1,1,1 MINUS ALL 1 = 1,1). INTERSECT ALL keeps the smaller of the two occurrence counts.

c1455.back: 19c: ORA-00933 SQL command not properly ended (use MINUS). 21c and 23ai: EXCEPT is a synonym for MINUS, and EXCEPT ALL for MINUS ALL.

c1456.front: A MINUS (SELECT with NULL) vs NOT IN (SELECT with NULL)?
c1456.back: MINUS: the NULL removes only the row with NULL from A, the rest stays. NOT IN: returns nothing, because a comparison with NULL gives UNKNOWN.

c1457.front: ORA-01789 in (id, name) MINUS (id): is adding NULL in the second part a fix?
c1457.back: The query runs, but (id, name) never equals (id, NULL), so nothing is subtracted. Use the same columns in both parts (join the name in), or do the MINUS on the key alone in an IN subquery.

c1458.front: A UNION ALL B UNION C: do the duplicates from A and B stay?
c1458.back: No. In order: (A UNION ALL B) UNION C, and the final UNION removes duplicates from the whole result so far. On the other hand, A UNION B UNION ALL C keeps all rows from C.

c1459.front: Which pairs of column types match in a compound query?
c1459.back: Those from the same type group: NUMBER/BINARY_DOUBLE, CHAR/VARCHAR2, DATE/TIMESTAMP, and NULL matches everything. NUMBER or DATE with a string literal: ORA-01790 (no automatic conversion).

c1460.front: ORDER BY UPPER(name) at the end of a UNION?
c1460.back: ORA-01785: ORDER BY item must be the number of a SELECT-list expression. Only result column names/aliases or positions are allowed. To sort by an expression, wrap the whole compound query in an inline view.

c1461.front: (SELECT ... ORDER BY x) UNION SELECT ...: is that allowed?
c1461.back: No: ORA-00907 missing right parenthesis. ORDER BY is allowed in an inline view in FROM, but the result of a compound query has no order without a final ORDER BY anyway.
c1461.try_sql:
-- ORDER BY in parentheses in a part of a compound query: error
SELECT customer_name FROM customers
UNION
(SELECT last_name FROM employees ORDER BY last_name);
